subject: Post-demo: procurement preflight — econ sponsor confirmation & SLA waiver request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.m@bioclinic.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@bioclinic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement preflight — econ sponsor confirmation & SLA waiver request

Hi Asha / Tom — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can preflight procurement before you loop in legal/procurement: 

What we covered
- Demo: inference latency and cost profile for your 3k concurrent users scenario
- Data controls: VPC + customer-managed keys shown; audit logs demoed
- Pricing: pilot pricing + committed tier options (estimate attached in the one-pager)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the economic sponsor for this deal (name & best email) so we can align contracting and discount approvals?
2) Procurement will likely request our SOC2 report and security questionnaire — I attached a lightweight pack we typically send. Please tell us who the procurement contact will be and expected timeline.
3) One procurement ask flagged in the call: Bioclinic needs a 99.95% SLA for the pilot window. That is above our standard pilot SLA. If you confirm the buyer and procurement timeline, I will open an internal SLA exception request (and include requested duration / metrics).

I'll hold on the formal MSA redlines until we know: a) econ sponsor, b) procurement lead, c) whether they require a temporary higher SLA.

Proposed next steps
- Asha/Tom: share econ sponsor + procurement contact by EOD Tue 5/24
- We: prepare a short exception request + draft MSA with redlines for your review
- 1:1 follow-up if procurement asks for additional evidence (SOC2 + keys on hand)

Attachments: Procurement_Timeline_OnePager.pdf (pdf), Bioclinic_Security_Questions.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Asha Menon <asha.m@bioclinic.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@bioclinic.com>, procurement@bioclinic.com
Date: 2027-05-22T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement preflight — econ sponsor confirmation & SLA waiver request

Jonas — great session, thanks. Quick answers: 

- Econ sponsor: Priya Shah (CFO) — priya.shah@bioclinic.com. She asked us to get a clear procurement timeline and any exceptions documented up front.
- Procurement lead: procurement@bioclinic.com (cc'd). They asked for the SOC2 and the filled security questionnaire (attached).
- SLA: Priya would like 99.95% during a six-month pilot. If Redwood can accommodate that rate for the pilot we can expedite internal approval. If not, we need to know the delta and any compensating credits.

We attached the security questionnaire the procurement team completed during the call. Expect a separate email from procurement with any contract boilerplate they require.

Best — Asha
Asha Menon
Head of Product Partnerships, Bioclinic Health
asha.m@bioclinic.com

Folks — forwarding Bioclinic's reply (below). Procurement wants 99.95% for a 6-month pilot and Priya Shah is the econ sponsor. Procurement attached their filled questionnaire and will send contract boilerplate.

Short ask from sales: can we get an internal pre-approval for a temporary pilot SLA exception to 99.95% and a one-time courtesy discount (we're proposing 15% off pilot list price) to speed approval? If legal needs to tweak the MSA we can queue that, but procurement is asking for the SLA + a high-level commitment now.

Why this is time-sensitive
- They indicated prioritization: Priya will fast-track if we can meet the SLA/discount ask.
- If we wait for standard review cycles we risk slipping into Q4 procurement calendar.

Attachments received from Bioclinic: Bioclinic_Security_Questions.xlsx
Attachments for internal review: Draft_MSA_redlines_jonas_v1.pdf

Could Marissa or Lauren weigh in on:
- Risk tolerance for short pilot SLA bump to 99.95% (duration: 6 months)
- Whether a 15% pilot discount is approvable by Rev/Ops, or if we should route to Sales Ops for a formal discount approval

Thanks — Ben

Thanks for the context — quick internal decision: 

- APPROVED (conditional): We can grant a temporary SLA exception to 99.95% for a 6-month pilot, subject to:
  * A risk acceptance note signed by Rev Ops and Security outlining compensating controls (we'll use the one-pager + SOC2 evidence).
  * A cap on financial exposure: uptime credit schedule limited to pilot-value not exceeding 6 months of committed fees.
  * Legal to confirm specific MSA redlines (I assigned the Draft_MSA_redlines_jonas_v1.pdf to Legal queue).

- Discount: 10% pilot-only courtesy discount approved. Anything >10% requires Sales Ops approval and a Rev Ops review.

Ben/Jonas — please route the MSA redlines to Legal and attach the SOC2 evidence. I'll notify Revenue Ops and tag Sales Ops if they want to push to 15%.

Lauren Bishop
VP Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
